extractedClaims.text: Gartner predicts AI's impact on global jobs will be neutral through 2026.

extractedClaims.text: Organizations that prioritize developing human capabilities alongside AI skills are nearly twice as likely to have workers who feel their work is meaningful.

extractedClaims.text: Around 70% of highly AI-exposed workers are employed in jobs with a high average capacity to manage job transitions if necessary.

extractedClaims.text: 6.1 million workers, primarily in clerical and administrative roles, lack adaptive capacity due to limited savings, advanced age, scarce local opportunities, and/or narrow skill sets.

extractedClaims.text: Of the workers lacking adaptive capacity, 86% are women.

citation.quote: Of these workers, 86% are women.

extractedClaims.text: Highly AI-exposed occupations with low adaptive capacity make up a larger share of total employment in college towns and state capitals, particularly in the Mountain West and Midwest.

extractedClaims.text: Policymakers concerned about AI’s job displacement potential may wish to focus attention on workers with the weakest adaptive capacity, who are likely to face the highest welfare costs if displaced.

extractedClaims.text: Workers with greater savings weather economic storms more effectively.

citation.quote: Workers with greater savings weather economic storms more effectively. Chetty (2008) shows individuals with greater liquid savings are less financially distressed after job loss and take longer to find better-matching jobs, while low-wealth individuals are forced into lower-quality employment.

extractedClaims.text: Workers aged 55 to 64 who experienced job loss during the Great Recession were about 16 percentage points less likely than those aged 35 to 44 to find employment afterward.

extractedClaims.text: Workers in more densely populated areas face lower costs to make work transitions compared to those in low-density areas.

extractedClaims.text: Workers with the highest AI exposure rates have characteristics that give them higher capacity to navigate job transitions successfully, finding new employment quickly and minimizing earnings losses after job displacement.

extractedClaims.text: A large group of 26.5 million workers are concentrated in high-exposure occupations with strong pay, financial buffers, diverse skills, and deep professional networks.

extractedClaims.text: Roughly 6.1 million workers face both high exposure to LLMs and low adaptive capacity to manage a job transition.

extractedClaims.text: There is a positive correlation between AI exposure and adaptive capacity, as higher exposure generally corresponds with higher adaptive capacity.

citation.quote: the interplay of adaptive capacity scores with AI exposure scores reveals a positive correlation: As exposure increases, adaptive capacity generally increases as well.

extractedClaims.text: Routine office jobs, such as those of door-to-door sales workers and news and street vendors, show the least adaptive capacity among the occupations in the top quartile of AI exposure.

extractedClaims.text: The adaptive capacity of different workers within the same occupation can vary substantially.

extractedClaims.text: There remains significant uncertainty about both the extent to which AI will impact labor markets as well as the differential burdens and opportunities that AI can bring for affected workers.

extractedClaims.text: The index of adaptive capacity may be less informative when AI affects clusters of related occupations simultaneously, as structural job availability may matter more than individual-level characteristics.

citation.quote: Moreover, if AI fundamentally transforms the economy on a scale comparable to the industrial revolution (as some experts have suggested could be possible), it could make entire skill sets redundant across several occupations simultaneously.

extractedClaims.text: The index of adaptive capacity may be most informative when displacement is relatively isolated, such as when a worker loses their job but related occupations remain stable.

citation.quote: The index may be most informative when displacement is relatively isolated—for example, when a worker loses their job but related occupations remain stable.

extractedClaims.text: There are numerous factors that affect a worker’s ability to navigate technological displacement, and many of these factors are not captured in the index of adaptive capacity.

citation.quote: However, there are dozens of confounding individual, firm, occupation, and local labor market factors that will ultimately shape a worker’s ability to navigate technological displacement, and that evade measurement in this index.

extractedClaims.text: The result that AI exposure is positively correlated with measures of adaptive capacity appears robust across many alternative ways of computing the index.

extractedClaims.text: There are large zones of strong resilience to job loss across the workforce, as well as concentrated pockets of heightened vulnerability if displacement were to occur.

extractedClaims.text: Adaptability analysis can provide a starting point for policymakers to better understand who may be most in need of better support to weather job transitions.
